- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., > +1.5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.3), model frequently underestimates upward momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 3–5 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile; add 0.3–0.8% buffer to early forecast points.  
- When sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak, model often fails to recognize the reversal; delay peak forecast until 2–3 days later and raise slope gently.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate volatility in the final 5–7 days; cap forecast rise in last 5 days to avoid over-optimism.
